summary: Gherardo De Vincentiis was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied under Giacomo Lignana circa 1864–1870 and was appointed incaricato at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" in 1878.

Gherardo Gnoli worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and religious studies. He studied at Sapienza University of Rome under Antonino Pagliaro (~1954–1958). He held posts at Naples "L'Orientale" (1965–1993) and Sapienza (1993–2008), and directed Serie Orientale Roma (~1979–2012).

Ghulam Yazdani worked in Indology and archaeology. He studied at Aligarh Muslim University under C. F. Andrews, Mohammad Ishaq, and Nazir Ahmad Dehlvi. He taught at St. Stephen's, Rajshahi, and Government College, Lahore, before directing archaeology in Hyderabad (~1914–1943).

Giacomella Orofino specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Raniero Gnoli, earned degrees from University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Sapienza University of Rome, and served as Associate Professor at Naples "L'Orientale" (1998–2017).

Linguist Giacomo Devoto studied at Pavia, Berlin, Basel, and Paris under scholars including Schulze, Lüders, Pokorny, Wackernagel, and Meillet. He held professorships at the universities of Cagliari (1927), Florence (1924, 1928, 1939), and Padua (1930).

Giacomo Lignana worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Turin and under Christian Lassen and Friedrich von Spiegel. He held posts at Turin, Naples "L'Orientale", the University of Bologna, Naples Federico II, and Sapienza University of Rome.
Gianpaolo Vetturini is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD at the University of London under the supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

Giei Honda was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1910–1914). He served as lecturer and assistant professor at Kyoto University (1929–1948), and later held professorships at Rissho University and Aichi Bunkyo Women's College.
Giho Okada was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Komazawa University under Kaiten Nukariya. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University.

Gikyo Ito specialized in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga and Yasusaburo Sakaki, subsequently teaching there (1940–1972, professor 1968–1972) and later at Kyoto Sangyo University (1977–1980).

Gil Fronsdal is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at Stanford University (~1989–1998), studying under Carl Bielefeldt, Bernard Faure, and Jan Nattier. He has been affiliated with the Insight Meditation Center and Sati Center for Buddhist Studies.

Gilam Seok is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a bachelor's at Hankuk University of Foreign Studies and a doctorate at Dongguk University WISE Campus. Posts include Dongguk University WISE Campus and membership at Geumgang University.

Gilbert Lazard was a linguist and specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studying at the École Normale Supérieure (1940), he held posts at the University of Paris (~1958–1980) and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1969–1990).

Gilbert Slater was a historian and Indologist who earned his doctorate from the London School of Economics. He served as Principal of Ruskin College (1909–1915) and was appointed the first Professor of Indian Economics at the University of Madras in 1915.

Gilbert Zhe Chen is a scholar of Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history. He earned his PhD at Washington University in St. Louis (2012–2019) and became an Associate Professor at Towson University in 2019.

Gilberte de Coral-Rémusat was a scholar of Indology and archaeology. She studied at the École du Louvre (~1924–1928) and École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1924–1929) under Jean Przyluski, Paul Pelliot, and Paul Masson-Oursel.

Gilles Tarabout is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied under Madeleine Biardeau. In 2004, he was attested as a senior fellow at the CNRS, member of EHESS, and exchange program director at the Fondation Maison des Sciences de l'Homme.

Gillian (Jill) R. Hart worked in linguistics and Indology. She studied at Reading, Lady Margaret Hall, and Oxford, where she studied under Thomas Burrow. She served as Lecturer in Classics at Aberystwyth (1960–1969) and Lecturer at Durham University (1969–1993).
Gillian Evison is an Indologist who held posts attested at the Indian Institute, Oxford (1992) and the Bodleian Library (1993–1998).
Gin Ling Liu is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2008) under the doctoral supervision of Jing Yin and studied with traditional teacher Hsing Yun.
